exposure: Referral to a tertiary care center for obstetric emergencies
outcome: Maternal complications (postpartal hemorrhage, septicaemia, wound gaping, puerperal pyrexia, maternal deaths)
Mode of delivery (caesarean section, normal vaginal delivery)
Neonatal outcomes (NICU admission, shifted to mother-side)
cohort: The study included all referred obstetric emergency cases with gestational age greater than 24 weeks during the antenatal and intranatal periods.
finding: Among 1470 delivered referred cases, 39.52% delivered by caesarean section, 55.44% by normal vaginal delivery, with specific rates of postpartal hemorrhage (5.66%), septicaemia (1.0%), wound gaping (4.33%), puerperal pyrexia (3.5%), maternal deaths (0.01%), and 17% neonatal NICU admissions.
